items.fromString: HMSIDM: Build a Playbook Playground Service for Console
items.toString: HMSIDM: Build a Playbook Playground Service (PPS) for Console

items.fromString:
h4. *Goal:*
 * Implement a HMS service called Playbook Playground which will allow us to send Playbooks via the service to the Cloud VMs (rhc-worker-playbook).

*Acceptance Criteria:*
 * You should be able to use a command line client to send a playbook in yaml format to the Playbook Playground service.
 * The Playbook Playground service should take care of sending the playbook to the recipient cloud VM and execute it there.

h4. *Open questions:*
 * *A lot, see sub-tasks ;)*

 

For a idea what we build:

[https://raw.githubusercontent.com/RedHatInsights/playbook-dispatcher/master/docs/communication.svg]
 

Replace remediation with Playground Playground Service (PPS).

*Goal:* 
 * As a developer I want to add metrics easily to the backend service.

*Acceptance Criteria:*
 * Metrics endpoint is configured from clowder.
 * Metrics are exposed, and can be retrieved by curl.
 * (wish) unit tests.
 * A prometheus container can be started and pull the metrics when running from the workstation.
 * (wish) a grafana container can be started and used to create dashboards.

{*}UPDATE{*}: Added items to get local infrastructure usable from the workstation.

items.fromString:
*Goal:* 
 * As a developer I want a starting point to build a backend service for console.dot platform

*Acceptance Criteria:*
 * [x] It uses echo framework.
 * [x] It uses viper for the configuration.
 * [x] I can design first the api and generate the handler boilerplate from it.
 * [x] the business logic is decoupled from the handler which is generated by the boilerplate.
 * [x] It includes the scripts into the repo to integrate with the pipelines.
 * [x] It has support for golangci linter and other additional linters by using pre-commit; and the configuration for golangci linter.
 * [x] I can deploy the result into the ephemeral environment (the current local state).
 * [x] It reads the configuration from the clowder configuration injected.
 * I can run unit tests from the workstation (cli and vscode ide).
 * [x] It has support for vscode debug launcher (open to add additional supports); and I can debug unit tests.
 * [x] I can build and push container images to my quay.io account (expiring in 1 hour by default).
